static_findings.finding: Pre-lock samples can be serialized out of sample order
interleaving: Thread A captures BOOTTIME t1 then is descheduled before retained lock.
Thread B captures t2 > t1, acquires retained lock, updates last_checked_ns=t2 and releases.
A acquires retained lock with its earlier t1; original now < last_checked_ns branch rejects and fences although CLOCK_BOOTTIME did not regress.

static_findings.finding: Refresh can upgrade a transient retained-lock contention to whole-feed fence
static_findings.detail: refresh's final live.current() uses cache.current's try_lock. An original WouldBlock produces Unavailable without fencing inside cache, but refresh returns Err, the worker returns and its original FenceOnDrop fences the shared feed.

clock_and_sync_scope.projection: Root preserves Unix sub-ms phase by subtracting unix_ns mod 1ms from BOOTTIME anchor. Same-boot project uses max(previous_unix + elapsed, sampled_realtime), hence its offset and ceil receiver projection do not inherently regress.
clock_and_sync_scope.sync: ConsumerSyncJob's revocation_head/update_revocations do not invoke the same LiveRoot clock; ensure_live_state is local journal validation. Original Root frontier CAS uses its distinct fixed consumer lane, actual pidfd/deadline and Root clock. No direct consumer-sync -> local cache clock -> consumer-sync lock cycle was found in this bounded review.
clock_and_sync_scope.not_excluded: Long original protected I/O or shared registry dispatch fence can delay the observation lane. This review has no runtime timing evidence and does not relax the 500ms age/deadline.
